support_text: In micropigs, folate deficiency alone reduced liver folates by one half, while ethanol feeding alone reduced methionine synthase activity and hepatic methionine, SAMe, and glutathione levels and increased lipid peroxidation. The combined treatment of folate deficiency and ethanol administration increased plasma homocysteine, liver S-adenosylhomocysteine, and urinary 8-hydroxy-2-deoxyguanosine (an index of DNA oxidation), increased serum aspartate aminotransferase activity, and promoted steatohepatitis.
